claim_boundary: Inherited-candidate means generic source appears in the selected GrapheneOS framework, not that a DiamaneOS FP6 build has passed. Hardware and Pixel-specific behavior requires the named build/device experiment.

selected_interfaces: android.hardware.security.keymint AIDL 3 default device and remotely provisioned component
android.hardware.wifi, hostapd and supplicant AIDL default

compatibility.result: stock system/vendor contract observed; selected GrapheneOS framework compatibility unverified
compatibility.rule: Treble/VINTF is a compatibility contract, not proof that the newer GrapheneOS framework works with this vendor image. Never bypass enforcement to make the build boot.

capabilities.basis: Generic GrapheneOS/AOSP framework capability; no FP6-specific hardware interface is intrinsically required.
capabilities.next_experiment: Build the selected framework and run early CTS plus exploit-mitigation/config audits.

capabilities.basis: Generic GrapheneOS framework/package features; product inclusion and profile behavior still need build validation.
capabilities.next_experiment: Verify package inclusion, permission enforcement and multi-user/profile cases on the candidate.

capabilities.basis: FP6 reference configuration defines AVB image keys and rollback locations, but GrapheneOS Pixel keys/layout are not portable and locked custom-key boot is untested.
capabilities.next_experiment: Generate dummy-key images, verify the complete AVB chain, then perform the separately authorized relock/rollback/recovery test.

capabilities.basis: The reference device lists 15 A/B OTA partitions and virtual A/B without compression. Pixel target-files and OTA assumptions are not portable.
capabilities.next_experiment: Build full and incremental target-files/OTAs, verify signatures and exercise slot, interruption and recovery behavior.

capabilities.basis: The FP6 exposes metadata/userdata partitions, but the selected vendor KeyMint/Gatekeeper and user/profile credential paths are unverified.
capabilities.next_experiment: Bind fstab/vold/KeyMint/Gatekeeper inputs and run the full encryption and credential matrix.

capabilities.basis: The selected locked stock build exposes hardware_keystore and app-attestation features but no strongbox_keystore feature; its device VINTF declares only the default KeyMint/RKP instances and no Weaver HAL. This agrees with the Fairphone product selecting non-SPU Gatekeeper.
capabilities.next_experiment: Keep StrongBox/Weaver-dependent product features disabled, verify TEE KeyMint/Gatekeeper and attestation behavior on the candidate, and reject any build that falsely advertises the absent interfaces.

capabilities.basis: The selected locked stock build's arm64 CPU feature line does not expose mte and all inspected memtag boot-control properties are absent. MTE cannot be inherited from Pixel configuration.
capabilities.next_experiment: Keep MTE-dependent UI and product declarations disabled; verify the candidate does not falsely advertise or require MTE after kernel and product integration.

capabilities.basis: The FP6 and Pixel trees sharing an Android 6.1 kernel family does not prove Pixel patches apply to the Qualcomm/Fairphone source, configuration, KMI or firmware interfaces.
capabilities.next_experiment: Classify each desired patch by generic-kernel versus Pixel-device dependency, port narrowly, build and regression-test it; reject any patch lacking a maintained FP6 path.

capabilities.basis: FP6 has Qualcomm/Fairphone-specific power, thermal and USB implementations and sysfs/controller nodes.
capabilities.next_experiment: Use the pinned Qualcomm implementations and FP6 device configuration, then run suspend, thermal, charging and USB mode tests.

capabilities.basis: Published USB software support does not establish an FP6 hardware data-line cutoff.
capabilities.next_experiment: Trace controller support and test data removal independently from VBUS on the candidate; describe software-only behavior if no hardware primitive exists.
capabilities.owner: debug exposure auditing and hardware bring-up

capabilities.basis: The reference build includes the Virtualization APEX and pvmfw partition, which is configuration intent rather than runtime evidence.
capabilities.next_experiment: Verify protected-VM capabilities, firmware compatibility and applicable virtualization tests on the candidate.

capabilities.basis: Stock VINTF declares AIDL 2 radio families for slot1 and slot2 plus Qualcomm IMS AIDL 16 instances imsradio0 and imsradio1. Those services are proprietary and declarations do not prove provider behavior.
capabilities.next_experiment: Bind the matching vendor services and run the provider-varied physical-SIM/eSIM voice, SMS, data, VoLTE, VoWiFi and 5G matrix.

capabilities.basis: Kernel source is published but camera userspace, algorithms, calibration and firmware are device/vendor-specific prebuilts.
capabilities.next_experiment: Bind matching blobs and the optional TCL algorithm interface only if required, then run the complete declared camera matrix.

capabilities.basis: Kernel and substantial HAL source is published. Stock VINTF confirms the Qualcomm Wi-Fi stack, Bluetooth HIDL 1.1, audio HIDL 7.1/effect 7.0 and Samsung-named NFC service; firmware, some userspace and exact candidate module ordering remain vendor-specific.
capabilities.next_experiment: Build every declared module, bind matching firmware/HALs and validate load, suspend/restart and functional matrices.

capabilities.basis: Pixel/Tensor firmware, device HALs and trust hardware are not FP6 components.
capabilities.next_experiment: Exclude them from the FP6 product and fail dependency validation if a selected framework component requires one without an FP6 implementation.

acceptance_rules.pixel_only: Any entry with pixel_source_only=true must be adaptation-required, unsupported or unverified; it can never be inherited-candidate without new device evidence.
acceptance_rules.hardware_claims: No capability becomes supported from source inspection alone; only the named candidate/device evidence may promote it.
acceptance_rules.vintf: Missing or incompatible required interfaces stop the affected port work; broad shims or disabled VINTF enforcement are not fallbacks.
